sections.heading: Basic Attack
sections.text: Perform up to 4 consecutive attacks, dealing Electro DMG .

sections.heading: Parry Stance
sections.text:
Hold Normal Attack to enter Parry Stance at the cost of STA.

 While active, Rover is immune to interruptions, takes 60% less DMG, and continuously consumes STA. Release Normal Attack to exit Parry Stance and perform Basic Attack - Riposte Strike, dealing Electro DMG .

 If an attack hits Rover during a certain period of Basic Attack - Riposte Strike, neutralize this attack and temporarily Stagnate the target before performing Basic Attack - Riposte Strike: Crumble, dealing Electro DMG .

 Press Normal Attack shortly after casting Basic Attack - Riposte Strike to cast Basic Attack Stage 2.

 Press Normal Attack shortly after casting Basic Attack - Riposte Strike: Crumble to cast Mid-air Attack - Havoc.

 In Parry Stance, use Dodge to consume STA to perform Dodge: Flicker, which can trigger successful Dodges during the action of this skill shortly after it's cast.

sections.heading: Mid-air Attack
sections.text: Consume STA to perform a Plunging Attack from mid-air, dealing Electro DMG .

sections.heading: Mid-air Attack - Havoc
sections.text: Perform up to 3 consecutive strikes, dealing Havoc DMG . Press Normal Attack shortly after casting Stage 3 of this skill to perform Basic Attack Stage 4.

sections.heading: Dodge Counter
sections.text:
Press Normal Attack right after a successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Electro DMG .

 Press Normal Attack shortly after to perform Basic Attack Stage 3.

sections.heading: Mid-air Dodge Counter
sections.text:
Press Normal Attack right after a successful Dodge in mid-air to perform Plunging Attack at the cost of STA, dealing Electro DMG .

sections.heading: Overshock
sections.text:
At max Electric Surge, Resonance Skill is replaced with Resonance Skill Overshock, dealing Electro DMG .

 Press Normal Attack shortly after casting this skill to perform Normal Attack Stage 4.

 This skill can be cast in mid-air.

 If Resonance Skill Overshock is cast by pressing the button, clear all Electric Surge to grant Resonators in the team 10% ATK Bonus for 20s .

 If Resonance Skill Overshock is cast by holding down the button, consume 60 points of Concerto Energy to deal damage, then clear all Electric Surge to enter Apex Resonance.

sections.heading: Apex Resonance
sections.text:
While in Apex Resonance, Resonance Skill Thrum of All Sounds is unlocked, which consumes 10% Thunder Rage per second:
 While on the ground, press Resonance Skill to launch up to 7 consecutive attacks:
 The first 3 stages: Thrum of All Sounds: Spectro, dealing Spectro DMG .

 The next 3 stages: Thrum of All Sounds: Havoc, dealing Havoc DMG .

 The last 1 stages: Thrum of All Sounds: Silencing Blade, dealing Aero DMG .

 While on the ground, hold Resonance Skill to cast Thrum of All Sounds: Aero, dealing Aero DMG and leaping into the air.

 While airborne, press Resonance Skill to perform up to 6 stages of Mid-air Attacks:
 The first 3 stages: Thrum of All Sounds: Havoc Mid-air Attack, dealing Havoc DMG .

 The next 2 stages : Thrum of All Sounds: Aero Mid-air Attack, dealing Aero DMG and healing all nearby Resonators in the team.

 - The last 1 stages: Thrum of All Sounds: Aero Plunging Attack, dealing Aero DMG . Press Resonance Skill shortly after landing to cast Thrum of All Sounds: Silencing Blade.

 Hold Resonance Skill in mid-air to cast Thrum of All Sounds: Aero Plunging Attack.

 Each time Thrum of All Sounds hits the target, Thunder Bane is triggered, dealing Electro DMG to the target within range, considered Resonance Skill DMG.

 While in Apex Resonance, press Resonance Skill shortly after casting a Basic Attack to chain into a specific Thrum of All Sounds skill based on the different Basic Attack Stages.

Rover can hold up to 120 points of Electric Surge.

 Electric Surge is restored when Intro Skill - Thunderous Fury, Normal Attack - Deterrence, Resonance Skill - Thunderclap, or Basic Attack - Repel deals damage.

sections.heading: Cons
sections.text:
Buffs are too low for them to have any synergy with anybody as of their release. A future DPS character will probably make use of their ability to apply lots of Electro Flare stacks (maybe an Electro Rage DPS), at which point they’ll finally see any meaningful use.

 Fairly long rotation for a Hybrid character.

 Outro buff expires on Swap. Unprecedented for a Negative Status character.

 In other words, basically a useless character right now. But that’s subject to change at least!

sections.heading: Review
sections.text: Electro Rover is a 5-star Electro Sword Hybrid character who applies Electro Flare and buffs Negative Status characters. They follow a simple rotation that involves building their Forte up to the maximum to cast an enhanced attack before switching out.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation
sections.text:
Electro Rover applies a total of 15 Electro Flare stacks: 10 via their Forte Skill, 5 via their Ultimate at S2. They access this Forte Skill by charging up Electric Surge, a 120-point Forte gauge that is restored via their Basic Attacks and Skill.
 Once this Forte gauge is full, they have 2 options: tap their Skill, which makes the team benefit from a 10% ATK buff for 20s while dealing some solid damage, and holding their Skill to enter a special state called Apex Resonance.
 Unfortunately, while Apex Resonance is meant to be a sort of Main DPS state where Electro Rover uses all of their elements accessed earlier in the story in order to deal damage at significant field time costs, they not only forfeit the party-wide ATK buff (which doesn’t mesh well with their Outro), they also spend way too long dealing objectively mediocre damage. Judging by this, they are best relegated to only tapping the Forte Skill, rendering this part of their kit nothing more than a gimmick used for Main Story content (meaning their S6 is also useless in practical gameplay).
 So as a Hybrid, what do they provide? On top of that 10% ATK buff and Electro Flare stacks mentioned earlier, their Outro also provides 25% all-type DMG Amplification to any character who inflicts a Negative Status, which is a buff that is lost on swap. Not only is this a minor buff, Electro Rover is our first Negative Status character whose Outro expires on swap, firmly cementing them as a Hybrid character.
 And… that’s it. Since their Sequences are free, we’ll mention them - aside from the S2 that applies extra Electro Flare, they’re only small personal damage or Interruption Resistance increases. S5 and S6 are also useless in practice, since they’re related to their Hold Skill. They can run the Moonlit Clouds Echo set for a higher amount of single-target buffs though!

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
sections.text:
If it wasn’t obvious, Electro Rover is essentially a completely useless character in the current meta. They are clearly awaiting an Electro Flare Main DPS who will take advantage of their ability to apply 15 Electro Flare stacks total (which is quite a lot) on top of their small buffs in order to gain any value in the meta.
 As things stand, since S0 Jianxin really isn’t the best F2P character ever created, they can serve as a replacement buffer for Hiyuki teams if one of the 6 or so better limited options aren’t available for her. But that’s assuming your Jianxin isn’t S2 or higher, which she may be.
 In conclusion, there is very little reason to bother with Electro Rover currently. They are awaiting a team that will be able to make use of their Electro Flare application. Let’s wait for that and hopefully their potential future use case will push them higher into the meta!

 Review
 Electro Rover is a 5-star Electro Sword Hybrid character who applies Electro Flare and buffs Negative Status characters. They follow a simple rotation that involves building their Forte up to the maximum to cast an enhanced attack before switching out.
 Key Mechanics & Rotation
 Electro Rover applies a total of 15 Electro Flare stacks: 10 via their Forte Skill, 5 via their Ultimate at S2. They access this Forte Skill by charging up Electric Surge, a 120-point Forte gauge that is restored via their Basic Attacks and Skill.
 Once this Forte gauge is full, they have 2 options: tap their Skill, which makes the team benefit from a 10% ATK buff for 20s while dealing some solid damage, and holding their Skill to enter a special state called Apex Resonance.
 Unfortunately, while Apex Resonance is meant to be a sort of Main DPS state where Electro Rover uses all of their elements accessed earlier in the story in order to deal damage at significant field time costs, they not only forfeit the party-wide ATK buff (which doesn’t mesh well with their Outro), they also spend way too long dealing objectively mediocre damage. Judging by this, they are best relegated to only tapping the Forte Skill, rendering this part of their kit nothing more than a gimmick used for Main Story content (meaning their S6 is also useless in practical gameplay).
 So as a Hybrid, what do they provide? On top of that 10% ATK buff and Electro Flare stacks mentioned earlier, their Outro also provides 25% all-type DMG Amplification to any character who inflicts a Negative Status, which is a buff that is lost on swap. Not only is this a minor buff, Electro Rover is our first Negative Status character whose Outro expires on swap, firmly cementing them as a Hybrid character.
 And… that’s it. Since their Sequences are free, we’ll mention them - aside from the S2 that applies extra Electro Flare, they’re only small personal damage or Interruption Resistance increases. S5 and S6 are also useless in practice, since they’re related to their Hold Skill. They can run the Moonlit Clouds Echo set for a higher amount of single-target buffs though!
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 If it wasn’t obvious, Electro Rover is essentially a completely useless character in the current meta. They are clearly awaiting an Electro Flare Main DPS who will take advantage of their ability to apply 15 Electro Flare stacks total (which is quite a lot) on top of their small buffs in order to gain any value in the meta.
 As things stand, since S0 Jianxin really isn’t the best F2P character ever created, they can serve as a replacement buffer for Hiyuki teams if one of the 6 or so better limited options aren’t available for her. But that’s assuming your Jianxin isn’t S2 or higher, which she may be.
 In conclusion, there is very little reason to bother with Electro Rover currently. They are awaiting a team that will be able to make use of their Electro Flare application. Let’s wait for that and hopefully their potential future use case will push them higher into the meta!
